claims.statement: OpenWiki's test suite is run by Vitest, using the vitest runner and @vitest/coverage-v8 as dev dependencies rather than any separate test framework.
Ink terminal-UI components are tested by rendering them with `render` from ink-testing-library and asserting on the rendered frame via `lastFrame()`.
`pnpm test` is a three-stage gate that runs typecheck, then build, then the coverage run in order, so a change must pass type checking and a full build before its coverage test run.
The `typecheck` script type-checks both the server project (tsconfig.json) and the browser/client project (tsconfig.client.json) with `tsc --noEmit`.
The `coverage` script runs `vitest run --coverage`, and `build` compiles both TypeScript projects and copies the visualize client assets.

Coverage uses the V8 provider with `all: true` plus an explicit include of `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}`, so files no test imports still appear in the report (as 0%) instead of being omitted from the denominator.

Coverage deliberately excludes files that emit no runtime JS or cannot run in a Node unit test — .d.ts, pure types.ts modules, the telemetry/index.ts barrel, the browser-only visualize/client.ts, and the Ink keyboard state machine setup/credentials/use-init-setup.ts — because their extractable logic lives in separate tested modules.
Coverage reporters are configured as text, text-summary, html, json-summary, and lcov.

Test discovery keeps Vitest defaults and adds one path-agnostic exclusion, `**/benchmarks/*/repo/**`, so a LEDGER benchmark under `evals/ledger/benchmarks/` whose reconstructed `repo/` working tree carries the upstream project's own `*.test.ts` files is never collected as this project's tests. The exclusion still applies even though the vitest.config.ts comment references the outdated `evals/keb/` path.

The test/ tree mirrors the src/ tree directory-for-directory, so each subsystem's tests live at the path matching its source (e.g. test/agent for src/agent, test/connectors for src/connectors, test/generation for src/generation, test/integrations for src/integrations).
Tests import source modules directly by relative path (e.g. ../../src/...), so a source module can be unit-tested through Vitest's transform without first building dist/.

The claims tests are split by the claims subsystem's internal boundaries: test/claims/core (resolver-agnostic mutation and error model), test/claims/brains/code (the code claim brain: paths, preflight, runtime, session, store), and test/claims/evidence/repository (repository evidence resource and resolver).

Connector tests keep cross-cutting machinery (config, fetch-with-resilience, MCP client/runtime, tools) at the top level of test/connectors and place each individual source under test/connectors/sources.

Per-source connector tests exercise the source through its ingest() entry point offline: they point $HOME at a throwaway temp dir, feed controlled API responses through a stubbed fetch, and assert on the request built and the normalized raw dump written to disk, with no real network call or OAuth token.

Failure-path tests inject faults with vi.mock plus a vi.hoisted counter that wraps the real module and throws on selected calls while otherwise delegating to the real implementation, as when the repository run test injects metadata-write and run-state write/removal failures.

Tests that exercise on-disk behavior stay hermetic by creating an OS temp directory with mkdtemp, redirecting $HOME/USERPROFILE or OPENWIKI_CONFIG_DIR into it, and restoring/cleaning up in afterEach, rather than mocking fs.
Tests that touch Mermaid rendering install jsdom window/document globals by calling ensureDomGlobals() from src/mermaid/dom-shim.ts.

A small number of files named *.e2e.test.ts drive a real vendor SDK path instead of a mock; gemini-enterprise-claude.e2e.test.ts exercises the real Anthropic Vertex SDK and real Mermaid DOM shim using a throwaway offline credentials file so no real token or network request is involved.

Two evaluation suites under `evals/` are separate from the Vitest unit suite: LEDGER under `evals/ledger/` (TypeScript, run via `pnpm run eval:ledger` / `tsx evals/ledger/run.ts`) and DeepSWE under `evals/deepswe/` (Python, run via `python3 evals/deepswe/run.py`); neither participates in the `pnpm test` typecheck/build/coverage gate.

LEDGER (Longitudinal Evaluation of Documentation Grounding, Evolution, and Revision) replays a benchmark's Git checkpoints, runs OpenWiki against each frozen source snapshot, and scores every current factual claim into exactly one state: supported, stale, invented (printed as `hallucinated` by the CLI), or unverified.

The LEDGER run-level score is opportunity-weighted claim health: supported current claims divided by all current claims across checkpoints, so stale, hallucinated, and unverified claims all lower it by remaining in the denominator.

LEDGER drives OpenWiki through its real `runOpenWikiAgent` entrypoint with `outputMode: "repository"`, running `init` at the first checkpoint and `update` at each later one with no user message, so update change-detection is driven purely by the real source deltas between checkpoints.

LEDGER benchmarks live under `evals/ledger/benchmarks/{calc,taskflow}/`; each benchmark directory holds a `benchmark.json` manifest (name, difficulty, ordered pinned checkpoint commits, and an optional semantic evidence map) plus a `repo.bundle` whose `sourceRepo` (e.g. `"./repo"`) points at a gitignored working tree that `ensureSourceRepoAvailable` reconstructs from the bundle when it is absent.

The `repo/` working tree that `ensureSourceRepoAvailable` reconstructs for a LEDGER benchmark can carry the upstream project's own `*.test.ts` files, which is precisely why the Vitest discovery exclusion `**/benchmarks/*/repo/**` exists.

LEDGER has its own TypeScript project config under `evals/ledger/tsconfig.json` (extending the root tsconfig with `noEmit`) and a dedicated typecheck script `pnpm run eval:ledger:typecheck`, plus a `reevaluate` mode (`pnpm run eval:ledger:reevaluate`) that re-scores a saved run without invoking OpenWiki again.

DeepSWE is a Python paired baseline-vs-OpenWiki harness that runs Codex on DeepSWE coding tasks in two conditions — `baseline` (task and repository only) and `openwiki` (OpenWiki restored/generated in an isolated clone, its managed instructions merged into root `AGENTS.md`, and `openwiki/` plus `AGENTS.md` copied into `/app`) — with the same tasks, seed, model, reasoning effort, attempts, and Harbor environment.

The DeepSWE `run.py` CLI exposes `prepare`, `baseline`, `openwiki`, `paired`, and `summarize` subcommands; `paired` runs both arms and summarizes them, pins reproducibility (DeepSWE commit, harbor/litellm/Codex versions, and a locally packed OpenWiki checkout), and records results to LangSmith via Harbor's `langsmith` plugin.

DeepSWE's own tests are Python `unittest` tests under `evals/deepswe/tests/` run in the pinned Harbor environment, not Vitest tests; because the harness is Python it has no role in `pnpm test` or the Vitest coverage run.
